requirementsKey.network: Sandbox can download public data and npm packages
requirementsKey.webgl: Headless Playwright Chromium can create a WebGL2 context (proved by tests/e2e/webgl-smoke.spec.ts, added in S01)
requirementsKey.supabase: Docker daemon running, local Supabase running (npx supabase start), and .env.local has NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
requirementsKey.realtime: Local Supabase Realtime service healthy (npx supabase status lists it) with public access disabled for private channels in supabase/config.toml; verified by npm run check:realtime
requirementsKey.stripe: Stripe test-mode keys (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) in .env.local and Stripe CLI installed and logged in for webhook forwarding

tasks.title: Scaffold, PWA shell, quality gates
tasks.acceptance: Next.js 16.3.x (App Router) + TypeScript 6.0.x strict + Tailwind 4 builds with the exact versions pinned in CLAUDE.md (three, @react-three/fiber and @react-three/drei pinned without ^); npm scripts dev, build, start, typecheck, lint (ESLint CLI with jsx-a11y and no-console), format:check (Prettier), test (Vitest), e2e (Playwright, specs in tests/e2e) and budget, each with one passing sample; Playwright projects 'mobile-390' (390x844, touch) and 'desktop-1280'; tests/e2e/webgl-smoke.spec.ts proves headless Chromium creates a WebGL2 context, with launch flags documented in README; a shared e2e fixture fails any test on a console warning or error (PERF-1) and provides an axe check that fails on serious or critical violations (A11Y-2); PWA manifest via app/manifest.ts (name 'Clout City: NYC', short name 'Clout City'), icons, installable, locked mobile viewport; bottom tab layout correct at 390px; one overlay layer system (named layers, reserved safe zones for HUD, sheets, toasts and banners) with screenshot and bounding-box tests at 390 and 1280 proving no overlap (UX-1); structured logger in src/lib/log.ts; supabase CLI added as a devDependency and supabase/config.toml initialised (no running stack needed); .gitignore covers env files, build output, test artefacts and the geo download cache.

tasks.title: Data, copy, formatters, and store
tasks.acceptance: /data folders for items, premium, events, jobs, venues, landmarks, geo, zones, audio, config (including config/perf.json with every budget from CLAUDE.md, config/theme.json palette tokens, config/realtime.json) and copy, each validated by a zod schema with a test; central copy file with slang-pack layer (test proves swapping the pack changes rendered text); one shared formatter module: money shown as whole dollars (GR-11) and counts via Intl.NumberFormat notation 'compact' (UX-2); a copy test fails if any copy string uses a superlative (cheapest, biggest, best, most, fastest) as literal text rather than a value computed from data (GR-11); Zustand store with localStorage persistence and schema version (test for persist and rehydrate).

tasks.title: Core engine
tasks.acceptance: Pure-function game clock (1 real min = 10 game min of passive time, pauses when tab hidden, 1x/2x toggle); actions fast-forward the personal clock instantly by their duration; the engine never reads the real clock (time is injected) and exposes city time (real New York wall-clock time) separately from the personal game clock; energy, hunger, mood decay with penalties at zero; action system with time, money, energy costs and stat effects validated in the engine; save/load with a schema migration test; unit tests for time math, action fast-forward, day and week rollover, insufficient funds, and city time across a DST change.

tasks.title: Geo pipeline and projection
tasks.acceptance: npm run geo:build reproducibly downloads pinned sources (NYC Open Data borough boundaries clipped to shoreline, NYC parks, Neighborhood Tabulation Areas, MTA static GTFS subway shapes and stops; OSM only for a layer no city source provides, kept in its own ODbL file) into a gitignored cache and writes simplified, quantized layers to /data/geo plus play zones (grouped NTAs) to /data/zones; output is deterministic (checksum test: same input gives byte-identical output); raw MTA files are kept unmodified in the cache and derived files are labelled derived; /data/geo/SOURCES.md lists each source URL, retrieval date, license or terms, transformations and required attribution text (MTA: not endorsed, no accuracy claim; OSM ODbL notice if used); one projection module (lat/lng to local metres, fixed origin) is shared by scene and engine; base geo gzipped size is within perf.json geoBaseGzKB; unit tests prove known coordinates land in the correct borough (Times Square in Manhattan, the Unisphere in Queens, Prospect Park in Brooklyn, a Bronx point, St George in Staten Island), an Upper Bay point is in no borough, and every subway station lies on a line.

tasks.title: 3D city base scene
tasks.acceptance: The react-three-fiber canvas is lazy-loaded with no SSR so the DOM shell is interactive before the 3D chunk arrives; borough land extruded from /data/geo, water plane, parks, subway lines as ribbons in our own colours with plain line letters and stations as markers (no MTA logos or bullets); toon shading via a shared gradient ramp and palette tokens from config/theme.json; camera rig with one-finger pan, pinch zoom and limited two-finger rotate and tilt, bounded to the NYC extent with zoom limits; frameloop is on demand (test hook frame counter shows zero frames over 2 s idle); zero console warnings with the pinned three version (if R3F triggers three deprecation warnings, pin three to the newest version that does not and record it in progress.md); required map attribution visible on the map; a test-mode hook exposes camera state and renderer.info; Playwright pans and zooms on mobile-390 and asserts camera state; draw calls and triangles at the default view are within the mid-tier budget.

tasks.title: Quality tiers and performance budgets
tasks.acceptance: A pure tier picker chooses low, mid or high from WebGL2 support, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency, renderer string and Save-Data/prefers-reduced-data, with every threshold in perf.json (unit tests per signal); the runtime steps down one tier via drei PerformanceMonitor when average FPS stays below the config floor, with hysteresis, and never auto-upgrades above the detected tier; a settings override is persisted; per-tier settings (DPR cap, shadows, outlines, building density, max visible avatars) come from config; npm run budget fails when shell JS, 3D chunk JS, total JS, base geo or district assets exceed perf.json (gzipped); npm run e2e:perf runs a cold load under the cc-mid-4g profile (4 Mbps down, 1 Mbps up, 150 ms RTT, 4x CPU) on the low tier and asserts shell interactive within budget and playable within budget (median of 3 runs), a warm load within budget, and draw calls and triangles per tier; any shadow uses PCFShadowMap, never PCFSoftShadowMap.

tasks.title: Tappable places, accessible Places panel, no-WebGL fallback
tasks.acceptance: Points placed by real latitude and longitude render as instanced pins, are tappable with an on-screen hit area of at least 44 px and open a place sheet stub; a DOM Places panel lists every place grouped by borough, is fully keyboard navigable, offers the same actions as tapping in 3D and announces selection (A11Y-3); when WebGL is unavailable or the context is lost, the app shows the Places panel and a static stylised fallback and stays playable, and recovers when the context is restored; Playwright taps a point in the canvas (screen coordinates from the test hook) and the same place via the panel, and a WebGL-disabled run completes a place selection; axe passes.

tasks.title: District buildings
tasks.acceptance: The geo script derives low-poly building masses from NYC Open Data building footprints (roof height field) for districts listed in config (Midtown, Lower Manhattan, Downtown Brooklyn and DUMBO, Williamsburg, Long Island City, Astoria, Flushing, Jamaica), simplified and merged per district per tier; elsewhere procedural low blocks by density; rendered as merged or instanced meshes with toon shading and flat emissive lit windows at night; no building carries a business name; each tier stays within its district-asset, draw-call and triangle budgets (npm run budget and e2e:perf); SOURCES.md updated.

tasks.title: Offline and caching
tasks.acceptance: A Serwist service worker precaches the shell, the 3D chunk, base geo and district assets for the detected tier, with versioned caches so updates replace old data; authenticated API responses are never cached; the service worker script is served with the no-cache headers from the Next.js PWA guide; Playwright loads the map, goes offline, reloads and completes a solo action; the warm-load budget passes.

tasks.title: Guest start on the 3D map
tasks.acceptance: Opening the root URL in a fresh browser shows the shell, then the playable 3D NYC map centred on the player's Queens start within the perf.json budgets, with no signup; a player avatar placeholder stands at the start point; play is local-only until the player answers the age check with 13 or older (S17); the session module exposes startSession() (anonymous Supabase sign-in, no-op when env vars are missing) which nothing calls in phase 1; S17 calls it only after a 13+ answer; a unit test calls startSession() directly with env vars present (mocked client) and absent; a Playwright test proves a fresh solo session makes no request to Supabase; HUD with stats, clock, money, clout and the goal line 'Make it in New York', placed in the overlay safe zones; page title and meta use the tagline 'Tap In. Blow Up.'; Playwright test confirms; no analytics, error-reporting or third-party request carries a persistent identifier before a 13+ answer.

tasks.title: Welcome card: consent and audio choice
tasks.acceptance: On first visit one welcome card sits over the already-loading map (the map keeps loading behind it and perf budgets still pass) with a consent checkbox linking Terms and Privacy and the audio choice 'Play our music' or 'I'll bring my own'; there is no age question on the welcome card or anywhere before solo play (test); consent version and timestamp and the audio choice are stored locally; no Supabase session is created by the welcome card; the form follows the shared pattern (noValidate, one zod schema, all errors at once inline with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, focus on the first invalid field, errors recomputed on change) (GR-1, GR-2, GR-8); no AudioContext is created and no audio is requested before the audio choice (GR-13); returning players never see the card again; existing e2e specs use a shared fixture that passes the card; Playwright covers the happy path, an empty submit, and an error that is fixed.

tasks.title: Audio channels and 'My own music'
tasks.acceptance: Audio system with separate music, sfx, ambience and voice channels plus master, each with its own volume; a one-tap HUD control and a settings toggle for 'My own music' mute in-game music only while sfx and ambience keep playing, with visible now-playing state and an accessible name; the choice is remembered per device (and synced to the account in S18c) and nothing overrides it; audio unlocks only from a deliberate tap on the audio choice or the sound control (GR-13); where the browser supports it, the audio session is set to mix with other apps (for example Safari's navigator.audioSession, checked against current docs) and sfx never take over the media session; all audio assets are CC0 or otherwise licensed and listed in /data/audio/SOURCES.md, with no third-party streams; audio loads lazily after the map is playable; unit tests for mixer state; Playwright proves no audio requests before the choice and that muting music keeps sfx enabled; mixing with a background music app on real iOS and Android is listed under Needs human review.

tasks.title: Guided first action and skippable tour
tasks.acceptance: A coach-mark tour over the live map (at most 6 steps, no tutorial screens, skippable, resumable from Help) leads the player through a first bodega purchase near their Queens start in about 20 seconds; a new player starts with at most 3 notifications, each meaningful (GR-9); no further gate or age check appears; Playwright completes the guided purchase and, separately, the skip and resume-from-Help path; a test proves no age question appears anywhere in the guided flow or before any solo action.

tasks.title: Boroughs, landmarks, and venues
tasks.acceptance: Five boroughs in data. Queens, Brooklyn, and Manhattan each have 8 invented venues with original names at plausible real coordinates (bodega, food spot, subway station, park or gym, coffee shop, thrift or boutique, club, job site). Landmarks at real coordinates with category, nameMode, and legalReviewed:false, at minimum: Brooklyn Bridge, Manhattan Bridge, Queensboro Bridge; Flatiron Building, Chrysler Building; Statue of Liberty (viewed from Battery Park), Washington Square Arch; Central Park, the High Line, Prospect Park, Flushing Meadows (Unisphere), Astoria Park; the Queens ballpark and the Brooklyn arena (generic labels); City Hall, Brooklyn Borough Hall, Queens Borough Hall; Grand Central, Penn Station, Jamaica Station; Times Square, DUMBO, Coney Island boardwalk, Flushing Main Street; 9/11 Memorial (memorial category). Landmarks show as placeholder markers in 3D until S07a and S07b. Bronx and Staten Island render as dimmed 'expanding soon' land teasing the Bronx ballpark and the Staten Island Ferry. Brooklyn and Manhattan unlock by clout level, with in-voice why-locked copy that is also in the accessible name. Validation tests: every landmark has a category and nameMode; branded names use generic labels; memorials have no flex, clout, emote, or event hooks; any superlative in venue copy is computed from data. Gating tests.

tasks.title: Low-poly landmarks I: bridges, buildings, stations, government
tasks.acceptance: Code-built low-poly models (procedural primitives, no downloaded models) in the toon style for every S07 landmark in the bridge, building, station and government categories, placed at real coordinates and orientation; generic-labelled landmarks show only their generic label; per-tier LOD via drei Detailed; per-landmark triangle budget from perf.json; merged or instanced where repeated; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier; each model is reachable from the Places panel.

tasks.title: Low-poly landmarks II: parks, monuments, stadiums, neighborhoods, memorial
tasks.acceptance: Code-built low-poly models for the remaining S07 landmarks; the Statue of Liberty is visible from Battery Park at the default zoom range; the memorial uses a muted palette with no emissive or animated effects, no emotes and no flex FX (test asserts no effect components are attached); per-tier LOD and triangle budgets as S07a; npm run budget and e2e:perf pass for every tier.

tasks.title: Transit and rush hour
tasks.acceptance: Walk, subway, and taxi with time and cost computed from real distances between points, per-mode speeds and fares in config; subway trips route via the nearest stations on the real lines in /data/geo, with walking legs at each end; travel fast-forwards the personal clock while the avatar animates along the route in 3D (subway along its ribbon) for at most the config animation length, and users with prefers-reduced-motion get an instant cut; rush hour (7-10am, 4-7pm) slows subway and drains mood; random MTA delay event hook; no MTA logos or official line bullets; unit tests for distance, routing, and modifiers.

tasks.title: Location action sheet, club door, landmark visits
tasks.acceptance: Tapping a venue or landmark in 3D or choosing it in the Places panel opens the same action sheet filtered by personal time of day and opening hours; closed venues show opening time; the club opens at night with a cover charge, a minimum clout level at the door with in-voice refusal copy, and a clout gain inside; non-memorial landmarks have a Visit action (time cost, mood gain) and a flexMultiplier from config for use by S13; memorials show a respectful info card only; tests.

tasks.title: Items, inventory, and shop
tasks.acceptance: 12 clothing and makeup items across 3 rarity tiers and 5 slots plus 3 gift types, all with currency 'cash', price, rarity, sellValue, cloutValue, statEffects; gifts are consumed when used on NPCs or yourself and cannot target another player; inventory and outfit equip; buy and sell with depreciation, prices displayed via the shared money formatter; schema validation and unit tests including insufficient funds.

tasks.title: Jobs and rent
tasks.acceptance: Four jobs per CLAUDE.md anchors (barista, retail, delivery with higher energy cost, junior dev gated by clout level with why-locked copy) with 4-hour shifts that fast-forward the personal clock; rent due every 7 game days; missed rent escalates to eviction and a move to cheaper housing; housing copy that compares rents is computed from data (GR-11); unit tests.

tasks.title: Economy simulation test
tasks.acceptance: A scripted bot plays 30 game days solo with a sensible strategy and ends neither bankrupt nor wildly rich (bounds in test); it saves roughly $150 per week and reaches the first apartment upgrade affordability between game days 10 and 14; any cost tuning needed to hit this is done in /data/config and logged; the bot also records its maximum clout and cash gain per action and per game day into a fixture used by S18c plausibility ceilings; test fails if balance drifts.

tasks.title: Clout, style, flex, levels
tasks.acceptance: Integer clout from item cloutValue (counts only while owned or equipped; a buy/sell loop cannot farm clout, proven by test), first paycheck, and a flex action with seeded-random viral chance weighted by outfit style score and the landmark flexMultiplier when flexing at a landmark; style score multiplies clout gains; six levels (Nobody, Local, Scene Regular, Known, Famous, Icon) in config with HUD progress; a level-up event is emitted; every clout change writes a typed ledger entry (source, amount, currency) so premium items (S25) plug in and can be capped and S18c can check plausibility without engine changes; unit tests.

tasks.title: Events
tasks.acceptance: Data-driven event engine with conditions (time, borough, location, stats, clout, items), weights, and choice outcomes; modal UI in the overlay system; 15 events in the voice of CLAUDE.md including MTA delay, rent hike, free pizza, club promoter offer, viral moment, 2 mild crime events, and at least 2 landmark-tied events; validation tests prove no event can fire at a memorial, no crime event can fire at a government building, and no event references alcohol, drugs, sexual content or gambling (content is all-ages); seeded-random tests.

tasks.title: Goals, grants, Icon moment, prestige
tasks.acceptance: Goals screen (first paycheck, first outfit, first landmark visit, first club night, first friend, level thresholds) with rewards and progress; every reward goes through one grant function that is idempotent (grant key), audited (grant log), eligibility-targeted and capped relative to the next progression goal from config, and granted value never counts toward goal progress (ECON-1, tests); reaching Icon shows a victory screen with a share hook and a prestige option (restart progress, keep cosmetics and premium items, earn a prestige badge; rules in config); tests; for players without a session, grants are local only and are re-validated by S18c if the player later gets a 13+ session.

tasks.title: 3D apartment and decor
tasks.acceptance: A low-poly toon 3D apartment interior for the Queens room and the Brooklyn 1BR upgrade (higher rent, more slots), within per-tier budgets; 6 decor items across rarity tiers placed in slots by tapping in 3D or through an equivalent DOM slot list (A11Y-3); colour variants have human-readable names (A11Y-1); locked upgrades show in-voice why-locked copy, also in the accessible name; home score feeds clout; Playwright places an item both ways.

tasks.title: 3D avatar and 'Make it you' creator
tasks.acceptance: A modular low-poly 3D avatar (code-built or CC0 parts listed in SOURCES.md) within per-tier triangle budgets, used on the map and in the apartment; guests start immediately with a randomized avatar and never meet the creator before first play; after the first action the creator is offered (skippable, always reachable from the HUD) with the flow Look, Traits, Dream (career path: influencer, streamer, artist/DJ, founder/hustler), Neighborhood roll (dice reveal among Queens start neighborhoods), Home; option and roll copy is generated from the same data that drives the options (GR-10); Hair, Facial hair, Accessories, Skin and Outfit are separate categories (GR-12); every swatch has a human colour name (A11Y-1); career path sets the goal line copy and a path-tagged bonus from config, and the S12 bot meets its targets for every path; native controls clicked in e2e; tests.

tasks.title: Age check at the moment it matters
tasks.acceptance: A pure age-rules module in src/engine maps an age band (unknown, under13, teen 13-17, adult 18+) to allowed features; the age question (neutral year-of-birth picker, no default, no hint of any threshold) appears only the first time a player tries a gated feature: being visible to or interacting with other players in the shared city, friend request, invite or share, chat, emotes, account upgrade, or a real-money purchase; it never appears before solo play or in-game cash purchases (test proves the S06 bodega flow and a full solo session never show it); only the age band and a timestamp are stored, never the birth year; under 13: solo play only, the shared city shows ambient life only, and every gated feature shows a friendly in-voice 'not available' message with no data collected and no Supabase session started (COPPA); 13-17: friends, friends-only chat, invites and shares allowed, visible in the shared city only to accepted friends, no stranger emotes, and a parental-consent notice before any real-money purchase; 18+: all features; unknown is treated like under13 for visibility; the band can be lowered by the player but not raised without support; the form follows the shared form pattern (GR-1, GR-2); unit tests for every band x feature cell and Playwright tests for each band's first gated tap; friend requests, invites, chat, emotes and roommate links are allowed only within the same band group (teen with teen, adult with adult); a cross-band invite opens the map with a friendly 'can't connect' message.

tasks.title: Core schema, RLS, age bands
tasks.acceptance: Migrations for profiles (age band set server-side from the S17 answer and changeable only downward by the player, age-check timestamp, consent version and timestamp, audio preference), saves, friendships, friend_boosts, roommates, referrals, live_stats, purchases, entitlements and grants, all with Row Level Security; purchases, entitlements and grants are readable only by their owner and writable only by the service role; a profile row is created only when a player answers the age check with 13 or older (no profile, session or personal data for under-13 or unanswered players); server helpers require_band(min) are called by every social, realtime and purchase RPC (13+ for friends, chat, invites, shares, referrals and purchases; 18+ for stranger visibility and stranger emotes) and tests prove an account below the required band is refused for each; a server-side function enforces one friend boost per sender per day; tests prove users cannot read or write others' private rows; a server helper same_band_group(a, b) is required by friend request, friend accept, roommate link, chat send, emote send and the friend fan-out in S29, with tests proving each refuses a teen-adult pair; if a player lowers their band, existing cross-band friendships are suspended server-side (hidden, not deleted).

tasks.title: Handles and public profile
tasks.acceptance: Guests get a generated safe handle from word lists in /data/copy; a handle form with live preview of the normalised handle, never a silent rewrite (GR-6), and the shared form pattern (GR-1, GR-2); server-side case-insensitive uniqueness, a filter for slurs, profanity, reserved and staff names and impersonation, and a rate limit on changes; the public profile exposes only handle, avatar, server-accepted level and career path, with no real-name field (GR-7); RLS and RPC tests including a filtered handle and a uniqueness race; handles exist only for 13+ profiles; a teen's handle is shown only to accepted friends.

tasks.title: Safety core: block, mute, report, moderation
tasks.acceptance: Migrations and RPCs for blocks (hide both ways), mutes, reports (reason enum, optional filtered note of at most 280 characters, context snapshot) and audited moderation actions, all with RLS (a reporter cannot read other reports; targets never see who reported them); content auto-hides after moderation.autoHideReports distinct reporters pending review; a /mod queue restricted server-side to accounts in MODERATOR_EMAILS with dismiss, warn, reset handle, suspend and ban actions; a /conduct Code of Conduct page; one reusable player actions component (Add friend, Mute, Block, Report) that every later player surface must use; the report form follows the shared form pattern; tests.

tasks.title: Cloud save sync and server plausibility
tasks.acceptance: Whenever a session exists, saves sync to Supabase (debounced, versioned, offline queue, with conflict handling by version and a server check) and restore on load; the server validates each save delta against ceilings derived from the S12 bot fixture times a config margin (clout and cash per action and per real minute, owned cosmetics against cash-shop and entitlement rules) and rejects and flags implausible saves; only server-accepted level, career path and cosmetics are ever shown to other players; audio preference syncs; tests prove a tampered localStorage save cannot change the public level or show an unowned premium cosmetic, and offline play queues and later syncs.

tasks.title: Account upgrade keeps progress
tasks.acceptance: After the first milestone the player is prompted to save progress via email magic link or Google, and is nudged again at each level-up until saved (GR-4), with a clear warning that clearing browser data loses guest progress; all guest progress, age band and consent carry over; the email form follows the shared form pattern; Playwright completes the magic-link flow using the local Supabase mail catcher; the Google button is present and its manual check is listed under Needs human review; the save-progress prompt and account upgrade are offered only to 13+ players; under-13 players are never asked for an email and see an in-voice note that progress stays on this device.

tasks.title: Invite link and friends
tasks.acceptance: Unique invite link with native share sheet; opening it lands on the map first (after the welcome card) with the referrer stored in the background, and an optional roommate-invite flag picked up by S21; friend list with send, accept, decline, mute, report, and block through the shared player actions component; friend prompts appear after first paycheck, first level-up, and first outfit purchase, capped per session; persistent 'Add friends' HUD button; no contact scraping; tests; invites, shares and friend requests require band 13+ (S17 asked at first tap, server-enforced via S18); under-13 sees the friendly not-available message.

tasks.title: Friends-only chat with a fixed daily limit
tasks.acceptance: One-to-one text chat between accepted friends only, only when both players are 13+ and in the same band group (server-checked); migrations for messages and chat_quota with Row Level Security (users read only conversations they are part of; no client writes to chat_quota); a server-side function sends a message and decrements quota atomically, allowing 10 text messages per player per day with a New York midnight reset and 140 characters max; the limit of 10 is read from config, applies to every player, and no purchase, reward, goal, referral, friend count, or account type can raise it; messages containing links, images, phone numbers, emails, or social handles are rejected server-side and do not use quota; unlimited emoji reactions and preset quick-replies that do not count toward the limit; a visible 'N of 10 left today' counter and an in-voice message when the limit is reached, with time until reset; report and block on every chat, and blocking hides the conversation both ways; tests prove the 11th message is refused, concurrent sends cannot exceed the limit, rejected messages keep quota, the reset happens at New York midnight, and users cannot read others' conversations.

tasks.title: Friend advantage
tasks.acceptance: A friend can send one daily boost (energy plus small clout) per day and the sender gets a small reward, enforced server-side and issued through the grant function; each friend adds a capped clout-gain bonus; two friends can link as roommates at the same apartment tier (including from an S20 roommate invite) and each pays a config percentage of rent, with no cash moving between players and the link enforced server-side; the S12 solo bot still meets its targets with zero friends; tests; roommate links require the same band group.

tasks.title: Share cards, photo snap, and deep links
tasks.acceptance: Branded 9:16 share cards via OG routes (footer 'Tap In. Blow Up. | Clout City: NYC') for level-up, borough move, viral flex, and landmark flex (landmark rendered in game art, never photos; never for memorials); a 'Snap' action renders the player's current 3D view into a card, where other players appear only as generic silhouettes with no handles; share links open a landing preview showing the real players-online count with one-tap 'Start your NYC story' that lands on the map with the referrer attached; snapshot and Playwright tests; sharing requires band 13+ (asked via S17 at first tap); under-13 can view but not share cards.

tasks.title: Referral reward
tasks.acceptance: When an invitee reaches their first paycheck, inviter and invitee each receive a referral-exclusive cosmetic item through the grant function; one reward per account or device; enforced server-side; fraud cases tested (self-invite, repeat device, reward replay); referral rewards apply only to 13+ players on both sides.

tasks.title: Heartbeat and live stats page
tasks.acceptance: A heartbeat RPC every 60 seconds (config) upserts player_state.last_seen for 13+ sessions; cached aggregate counters (players online = distinct last_seen within 2 minutes, total players, visits today, visits all time) refreshed every 30 seconds with no per-viewer DB query; counts never include NPCs, ambient pedestrians, or test bots (UX-3, test); all numbers use the shared compact formatter (UX-2); public /live page 'How New York is growing, live' with LIVE badge, 'updated Ns ago', and OG image; 'Post these numbers' button opens a pre-filled X post with tagline and referral-tagged link; no personal data exposed; tests; players-online counts only real 13+ sessions and never estimates or pads the number for players without a session (UX-3); for unknown and under-13 players, visits are counted only as anonymous increments with no cookie, device id or other persistent identifier (test inspects the request); /live labels the count 'players in the live city'.

tasks.title: Zones, shards, and server-authored presence
tasks.acceptance: Migrations and security-definer RPCs join_zone, move, set_activity, leave_zone with RLS; every RPC requires band 13+; adults (18+) join_zone into a shard of at most realtime.shardSize players (friends placed together when room allows) and receive a snapshot of adults seen within 2 minutes, capped, excluding blocked users both ways and ghost-mode players; teens (13-17) never join public shards: their events are sent only to their accepted friends' personal topics (player:<id>), and they receive only friends' events on their own personal topic, so adult strangers and teens never see each other; move validates the destination (known venue, landmark, station or in-zone point), the mode, borough unlock against the server-accepted level, and a minimum interval from config, then writes player_state and calls realtime.send with a private topic and an id-and-enum-only payload (from, to, mode, startedAt, durationMs); set_activity accepts only an enum; RLS on realtime.messages lets only shard members read a shard topic, only the owner read a personal topic, and no client insert; integration tests prove a non-member cannot subscribe, a client cannot broadcast, rate limits hold, blocked users never appear in each other's snapshots, a teen never appears in an adult stranger's snapshot or broadcasts (and vice versa), under-13 and unanswered players have no realtime access at all, and payloads contain no free text; teens call join_friends(), which requires band 13-17 and returns a snapshot of online accepted friends in the same band group seen within 2 minutes, excluding blocked and ghost-mode players.

tasks.title: Client realtime layer and graceful degradation
tasks.acceptance: A PresenceTransport interface in src/realtime with a Supabase implementation and an in-memory fake; an adult client joins the shard of its current zone, switches zones on travel, re-joins with exponential backoff after disconnect, leaves or pauses when the tab is hidden, and refreshes the access token on expiry; with env vars missing, offline, or Realtime unreachable the city stays fully playable solo with an honest 'You're offline' or 'City is quiet' status and no error toasts or console errors; unit tests with the fake transport for join, switch, reconnect and degrade; integration test against local Supabase; with band unknown or under13 the client never connects to realtime and shows the city as ambient-only with honest copy; teens subscribe only to their personal topic.

tasks.title: Other players and ambient life on the 3D map
tasks.acceptance: Other players render as instanced low-poly avatars (billboards on the low tier) capped at the per-tier max visible, nearest first, interpolating movement intents along the same routes as S08; optional handle labels with a settings toggle; a 'N people here' count from the snapshot only (UX-3) using the shared formatter; scripted ambient pedestrians are visibly different from players, never selectable as players, and never counted (test); every player avatar is also listed in the Places panel venue occupant list (A11Y-3); per-tier draw-call and triangle budgets still pass with the max visible players; a two-browser Playwright test proves adult player B sees adult player A arrive at a venue within 3 seconds, and a second test proves two teen friends see each other arrive; teens see only their accepted friends plus ambient life; a two-browser test proves an adult stranger and a teen never see each other.

tasks.title: Player surfaces, privacy, and ghost mode
tasks.acceptance: Tapping another player's avatar or occupant-list entry opens a player card showing only handle, avatar, server-accepted level and career path, with the shared player actions (Add friend, Mute, Block, Report); block removes both players from each other's snapshots and renders immediately and server-side thereafter; mute hides that player's avatar and emotes locally and persists; ghost mode (settings and HUD) removes the player from snapshots and stops their broadcasts server-side; the app never requests geolocation (test asserts the permission is never queried); two-browser Playwright tests for block, mute, report and ghost mode; axe passes; a teen's player card is reachable only by accepted friends; tests prove a stranger cannot open it; block between teen friends removes them from each other's personal-topic fan-out (test).

tasks.title: Preset emotes between players
tasks.acceptance: A fixed set of preset emotes, between adults (18+) in a shard or between accepted friends of any 13+ band (never between a teen and a stranger, test), from /data/copy (for example wave, hype, dap), sent through a server RPC with a per-sender rate limit from config and delivered as an enum to the adult shard topic, or for teens only to the recipient friend's personal topic; no free text, no custom content, no voice; emotes from muted or blocked players never render; emotes are disabled at memorials; emotes never count toward or interact with the chat quota; tests for the rate limit, the block and mute filters, and memorial suppression.

tasks.title: City-time live events and calendar
tasks.acceptance: Scheduled live events defined in /data/events/live keyed to city time (real New York time, with server time offset when online and device time offline), including a weekly club night and at least 4 calendar dates with generic names for trademarked events; the map shows upcoming events with a countdown; event bonuses come from config and are issued through the grant function (ECON-1); attendance counts shown to players come from real presence only (UX-3); no event at memorials; unit tests for scheduling across DST and for offline behavior; live-event content is all-ages.

tasks.title: Realtime load, cost, and abuse test
tasks.acceptance: A script (npm run sim:realtime) runs at least 50 simulated clients against local Supabase across several zones and measures messages per player-minute, join rate and snapshot latency; a test fails if messages per player-minute exceed realtime.budgetMsgsPerPlayerMinute in config or if any client exceeds server rate limits without being refused; the run writes a cost projection (monthly messages and connections at 100, 1,000 and 5,000 average concurrent players, using the Supabase pricing recorded in CLAUDE.md) to progress.md; abuse cases tested: rapid move spam, zone-hop spam, joining a full shard, and reconnect storms; abuse cases also include a client claiming a higher age band and a teen attempting to join a public shard; teen personal-topic fan-out is capped by realtime.maxFriendFanout (config, default 50) and projected separately.

tasks.title: Premium catalog and clout rules
tasks.acceptance: /data/premium holds at least 8 premium items (outfits, apartment themes, profile badges, share-card frames) across rarity tiers, each with currency 'usd', a price tier from config, cloutValue, and styleValue; premium items cannot be bought or sold for in-game cash, have no sellValue, and cannot be transferred; total clout from premium items is capped by premiumCloutCap in config; premium store screen shows clear USD prices and owned state (purchase button wired in S26); S12 simulation extended so a bot owning every premium item stays within balance bounds and cannot reach Icon on premium clout alone; tests.

tasks.title: Stripe Checkout and entitlements
tasks.acceptance: Stripe Checkout in test mode only, with the API version pinned to the one in the installed stripe-node; buying requires a saved account (guests are prompted to save progress first) and the server requires band 13+ before creating a session; under-13 is blocked; 13-17 must acknowledge a parental-consent notice first (recorded); 18+ proceeds; the Checkout session is created server-side from catalog prices (the client never sends a price); the webhook verifies signatures and writes purchases and entitlements idempotently (duplicate-webhook test); entitlements restore on sign-in on any device and premium cosmetics become visible to other players only once the entitlement exists; a refund webhook revokes the entitlement, its clout, and its public visibility; tests using Stripe CLI fixtures.

tasks.title: Copy, brand, and legal pages pass
tasks.acceptance: All player-facing text comes from the copy file with the slang pack applied to events, goals, prompts, emotes, chat quick-replies and limit messages, landmarks, live events, and share cards; welcome line and tagline present; placeholder Terms (all ages, with the age-band feature rules and a COPPA statement), Privacy (including 'No ad trackers, ever.' if still true), Purchases and Refunds, and Code of Conduct pages with a TODO for legal review; a credits page and in-app attribution for NYC Open Data, MTA (with not-endorsed and no-accuracy wording), OpenStreetMap with a link to openstreetmap.org/copyright and an ODbL download of any OSM-derived layer, and every CC0 or licensed asset.

tasks.title: Polish, smoke test, deploy readiness
tasks.acceptance: Loading, empty, and error states on every screen; offline solo play works and the shared city degrades honestly; every perf.json budget passes in npm run budget and e2e:perf; README covers setup, env vars, local Supabase and Realtime, Stripe CLI, data sources, quality tiers and budgets, moderation setup (MODERATOR_EMAILS), the production Supabase plan requirement and Realtime cost projection, adding items, premium items, events, live events, venues, landmarks, zones, and copy, and Vercel deploy steps (the deploy itself is a human step); end-to-end smoke test passes: open link, welcome card, land on the 3D map with no age question, first action, visit a landmark, buy item, level up, share card, and (when Supabase is configured) answering the age check as an adult and a second adult browser sees the player move.
